sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a word they haven't seen ('cherub'), and the wrong answers ('chariot', 'horse') are more natural than the right one. Nothing on the earlier cards lets a thoughtful baker reason their way to 'cherub'. It also hangs on a hard word.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: Card 2 (v21: kept the ways of the LORD, did not wickedly depart) and card 3 (v22: His ordinances are before me, did not disregard His statutes) ask about the same point, that David obeyed God's law. That is two questions on one point.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The question already says God's way is 'perfect', so 'flawless' is a near-synonym of the setup. The wrong answers ('hidden', 'far away') are the only negative-toned options and don't fit a praise verse, so the right answer stands out.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

sonnet.problem: The question says God 'subdues nations beneath him', and card 7 also says 'head of nations'. That puts the word 'nations' on screen before card 13, whose right answer is 'nations' (v49), so card 13 is partly given away.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
